# Page 2^page=2


# Page 3^page=3
• Launch: 2024 • Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Heavy Industries • Objectives: To expedite the adoption of EVs by providing upfront incentives for their purchase, as well as by facilitating the establishment of essential charging infrastructure for EVs • Coverage o Subsidies for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-ambulances, e-trucks, and other emerging EVs o Supports 24.79 lakh e-2Ws, 3.16 lakh e-3Ws, 14,028 e-buses • Financial Outlay: Rs. 10,900 crore over two years • Tenure: 1st October, 2024 till 31st March, 2026 Note: number of vehicles and the expenditure under EMPS-2024 for e-2w and e-3w being implemented for the period from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024 is being subsumed under PM E-DRIVE Scheme, therefore, effective period for the scheme will be two years.

# Page 4^page=4
• Key Features o Incentives: ▪ E-vouchers for EV buyers to claim demand incentives at purchase ▪ ₹3,679 crore allocated for demand incentives ▪ Additional ₹500 crore for e-ambulance deployment ▪ ₹4,391 crore for 14,028 e-buses in major cities ▪ ₹500 crore to promote e-truck adoption with scrapping incentives

# Page 5^page=5


# Page 6^page=6


# Page 7^page=7
o Infrastructure: ▪ Installation of 22,100 fast chargers for e-4Ws, 1,800 for e-buses, and 48,400 for e- 2W/3Ws. ▪ ₹2,000 crore allocated for Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) o Modernization of test agencies with an outlay of ₹780 crore o Procurement of 14,028 e-buses by public transport agencies - demand aggregation will be done by CESL in the nine cities with more than 40 lakh population namely Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Surat, Bangalore, Pune and Hyderabad. ▪ Priority for buses will be given to cities/states replacing old buses through authorized scrapping centers under MoRTH guidelines.
